players.seasonOutlook: Citron displayed a well-rounded skill set over her four seasons at Notre Dame and rose up draft boards after several other players -- including college teammate Olivia Miles -- elected to wait before going pro. However, Citron earned her status as a lottery pick, averaging 14.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.8 steals in 33.3 minutes per game during her time with the Fighting Irish, and she shot 37.7 percent from beyond the arc over the last three seasons. She should have plenty of chances to contribute for the rebuilding Mystics in 2025 after being selected at No. 3 overall, even though the team also selected Kiki Iriafen with the fourth overall pick. Citron will play alongside veteran Brittney Sykes in Washington's backcourt, and the rookie should have an opportunity to earn a starting role during training camp. Citron should be able to carve out ample playing time to begin her time in the WNBA, and her versatile skill set makes her an intriguing target in the mid-to-late rounds of fantasy drafts.

Elena Delle Donne officially announced her retirement during the offseason, but Iriafen should provide immediate frontcourt production for the Mystics as a rookie in 2025 after being selected with the No. 4 pick in the draft. Iriafen spent her first three collegiate seasons at Stanford but transferred to USC following a breakout junior year, and she remained dominant with the Trojans. Over the last two seasons, the 22-year-old averaged 18.7 points, 9.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 29.0 minutes per game, and she should see ample playing time as a rookie, even if she has to settle for a bench role behind Stefanie Dolson, Aaliyah Edwards and Shakira Austin. The Mystics struggled on the boards last year, so Iriafen should be able to provide a boost while also offering solid scoring potential, which could give her some fantasy upside.

The Wings struggled as a team for most of 2024, but McCowan remained consistent, averaging 11.7 points and 8.1 rebounds in 25.3 minutes per game. Dallas played without Satou Sabally and Natasha Howard over a month-long stretch early in the season, and McCowan was slightly more productive when those two were sidelined, as she averaged 12.6 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 27.7 minutes per game. Both Sabally and Howard departed during the offseason, so McCowan could see her role increase slightly in 2025, even though NaLyssa Smith is now part of the team's frontcourt. However, even if McCowan's production simply remains steady, she'll continue to be a reliable fantasy option in her age-28 season.

Wheeler has had decent fantasy value for most of her career, but her production fell off in 2024 after the Fever drafted Caitlin Clark. Wheeler started in just two of her 39 regular-season appearances and averaged 3.6 points and 1.8 assists in 14.0 minutes per game, her worst marks since 2015. She'll get a fresh start in her age-34 season, as she signed with the Storm this winter and will be in the mix for a starting role alongside Skylar Diggins-Smith after Seattle lost Jewell Loyd during the offseason. Diggins-Smith will be the primary scoring option in the backcourt, but Wheeler has usually been a reliable scorer throughout her career while providing modest numbers in secondary categories, so she should have a chance to regain a fantasy-relevant role in 2025.

Cunningham averaged double-digit points while serving mainly as a starter in the 2022 and 2023 campaigns, but she only had a part-time starting role in 2024 and showed some decline in the scoring column, averaging 8.4 points per game. However, she had some encouraging performances in secondary categories, as she averaged 3.9 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game, which were both the second-best marks of her career. The 28-year-old was traded to the Fever during the offseason, where she'll likely have to settle for a bench role on the team's revamped roster. Cunningham has shown enough production over the past few seasons to justify a mid-to-late-round flier in most fantasy drafts, but she could profile more as a streaming candidate due to the talent around her in Indiana.

Serving as a fill-in for Jordin Canada and Rhyne Howard, Jones started the first 24 games of the 2023 season and averaged 5.5 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 24.1 minutes per game. However, from Aug. 16 through Atlanta's playoff run, Jones played double-digit minutes only eight times over 18 contests and never saw more than 16 minutes in a game. The Dream made upgrades to their roster during the offseason, and Jones was left off the team's Opening Night roster. It seems likely that the No. 6 pick from the 2023 WNBA Draft will draw interest from other teams this year, but her fantasy upside could be limited.

After helping the Liberty win their first championship, Thornton was selected by the Valkyries during the WNBA Expansion Draft this offseason. Thornton has played for three teams (Washington, Dallas and New York) across nine WNBA seasons. She averaged 5.0 points and 3.0 rebounds in 18.8 minutes per game with the Liberty over the past two seasons, a significant decline compared to the 8.2 points and 4.9 rebounds in 26.4 minutes per game she averaged across six seasons in Dallas. Golden State's rotation is likely to ebb and flow throughout the season. Still, Thornton has a much clearer path to consistent minutes and usage with her new team than she did when competing for playing time with Breanna Stewart, Leonie Fiebich and Betnijah Laney-Hamilton.

Sims couldn't find much of a role during the 2022 and 2023 seasons, but her playing time increased in 2024 while suiting up for the Wings and Sparks. She made nine appearances (seven starts) while on a hardship deal with Dallas, averaging 17.2 points, 5.6 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 33.9 minutes per game, but her role declined once she joined the Sparks, as she averaged 9.8 points and 5.1 assists in 26.3 minutes per game over 15 appearances (10 starts) with the team. Her efforts were enough to earn her a one-year deal with Los Angeles during the offseason, but she may not see consistent scoring chances after the Sparks traded for Kelsey Plum. Even if she beats out Aari McDonald and Rae Burrell for a starting job, Sims doesn't profile as much more than a late-round fantasy option.

Parker-Tyus had a career-best year in 2023, averaging 15.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.5 blocks in 26.7 minutes per game. However, she started in just 11 of her 25 regular-season appearances in 2024 and averaged 9.2 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 19.7 minutes per game before missing the second half of the season due to an ankle injury. She signed a training camp contract with the Aces during the offseason but announced in April that she's pregnant and will miss at least the first three months of the regular season. She hopes to return to the court late in the year, but her fantasy potential is limited for 2025, even if she's able to make it back to game action this year. The Aces lost Alysha Clark during the offseason, so Kiah Stokes will presumably have a chance to take on a larger role in the frontcourt to begin the 2025 campaign.

After dominating at Louisville over her first three seasons in college, Van Lith transferred to LSU for the 2023-24 season and saw her production decrease. However, she transferred to TCU last year and bounced back while seeing time at point guard, and she helped lead the Horned Frogs to the Elite Eight in the NCAA Tournament. Van Lith was also part of the 3x3 Olympic squad for Team USA at the 2024 Paris Olympics, experience that could help her as she transitions to the WNBA. While the 23-year-old has had success on several different stages, she'll likely have an opportunity to learn and develop early in her WNBA career after the Sky acquired Courtney Vandersloot and Ariel Atkins during the offseason. Van Lith could develop into a solid WNBA player at some point, but her fantasy value as a rookie will likely be mainly as a streaming candidate.

Laney-Hamilton enjoyed the best two years of her career in 2020 and 2021, and while she hasn't been quite as productive over the three seasons since then, she's been remarkably consistent over that stretch. Across those three years, she's averaged 11.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 29.5 minutes per game, production that gives her a somewhat high fantasy floor. While the Liberty will retain most of their core players from the championship-winning group, Laney-Hamilton dealt with a lingering knee issue last year and underwent knee surgery in March that will likely force her to miss the entire 2025 season.

Martin was selected by the Aces in the second round of the 2024 WNBA Draft and saw relatively consistent minutes early in the season while the team dealt with injuries. However, her role dwindled down the stretch, and she averaged just 2.6 points and 1.6 rebounds in 11.5 minutes per game over 34 regular-season appearances. She was selected by the Valkyries during the expansion draft during the offseason and will have an opportunity for a fresh start during her second professional season. While the 24-year-old's playing time could increase as part of the league's newest franchise, she'll likely be behind Tiffany Hayes and Julie Vanloo on the depth chart, leaving her to compete with Juste Jocyte and Veronica Burton for minutes.

Carter began her career with a pair of productive seasons in Atlanta, but she was fairly unreliable with the Sparks in 2022 and failed to land a roster spot for the 2023 campaign. She joined the Sky in 2024 and had a bounce-back performance. She started in 20 of 33 appearances and averaged 17.5 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 26.0 minutes per game, but she didn't receive a qualifying offer from Chicago during the offseason, and she signed a contract with a team in Mexico in late April, signaling that she may not play in the WNBA in 2025.

Harrison missed the 2023 season due to a knee injury, but she made her Sky debut in 2024. She came off the bench for most of the year while Chicago prioritized the development of Angel Reese and Kamilla Cardoso. Although Harrison saw relatively consistent minutes off the bench, she wasn't a reliable fantasy option. She drew five starts late in the year while the team dealt with injuries but ultimately averaged just 6.5 points and 3.9 rebounds in 16.3 minutes per game over her 36 appearances, marking one of the worst overall performances of her career. The 31-year-old has had decent production at points during her seven WNBA seasons, but she's a free agent ahead of the 2025 campaign, and it's unclear whether she'll be able to land a starting role this year. Harrison would mainly have fantasy value as a streaming option if she doesn't start.

Taurasi is a WNBA legend, holding multiple scoring records, including all-time points and all-time three-pointers made. Her production has declined slightly in recent years, but she still averaged 14.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 29.0 minutes per game while appearing in 36 regular-season matchups in 2024, her age-42 season. She announced her retirement in February following a 21-year career, and Kahleah Copper should take on a leading role in the Mercury's backcourt moving forward.

After beginning 2024 as a reserve, McDonald carved out more playing time and earned a starting role in the 10 games ahead of the Olympic break. However, she missed most of the second half of the year due to foot and ankle injuries and was ultimately limited to just 26 appearances last year. The 26-year-old averaged 8.7 points, 3.7 assists and 2.0 rebounds in 21.8 minutes per game and appears to be back to full health after playing overseas this winter. Kia Nurse and Crystal Dangerfield are no longer with Los Angeles, but the Sparks acquired Kelsey Plum during the offseason and retained Odyssey Sims and Rae Burrell, so McDonald doesn't appear to be guaranteed a starting job in 2025. McDonald will have some fantasy potential if she starts, but she carries some risk after she had an inconsistent role last year.

After operating mainly as a starter earlier in her career, Nurse was limited to part-time starting duties with the Storm and Sparks over the last two seasons. Her production took a hit, as she averaged just 6.8 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 20.0 minutes per game. Nurse signed a one-year contract with the Sky during the offseason, and she'll likely have to compete for a starting role this spring. However, it wouldn't be surprising to see Nurse come off the bench since Chicago also brought back Courtney Vandersloot while acquiring Rebecca Allen during the offseason. Nurse has some scoring talent, especially from the perimeter, but it seems unlikely that she'll see enough playing time to be a reliable fantasy option in 2025.

Evans was a valuable asset off the bench for the Sky in 2023, and she began the 2024 season as a starter after Kahleah Copper was traded to Phoenix. Evans had decent fantasy production as a starter, but she lost her starting job to Chennedy Carter after just 12 games and never returned to the starting five. Evans' overall numbers decreased from the previous season, and she wasn't much more than a streaming option after shifting to a bench role. The 26-year-old will get a fresh start after being traded to the Aces during the offseason, but she'll presumably have to settle for a bench role behind Jewell Loyd and Chelsea Gray. Evans' scoring and passing abilities will make her a streaming candidate if some of her teammates are unavailable, but it seems unlikely that she'll be a viable season-long fantasy contributor.

Brown took a significant step during her first season with the Wings in 2023, averaging 7.8 points and 4.5 rebounds in 16.4 minutes per game. She appeared to be in line for an even bigger role last year since the Wings dealt with several frontcourt absences, but she regressed slightly, averaging 5.7 points and 3.1 rebounds in 13.2 minutes per game. The 28-year-old was traded to the Mercury during the offseason and will join a frontcourt that lost Brittney Griner but acquired Alyssa Thomas and Satou Sabally while retaining Natasha Mack. Thomas, Sabally and Mack will likely begin the year as starters, while Brown profiles as little more than a streaming candidate if she continues to play primarily off the bench.

After operating mainly as a reserve over the first four years of her WNBA career, Harris started in 38 of 39 regular-season appearances in 2024 and put up career-best averages of 10.5 points, 3.0 assists and 1.8 rebounds in 28.8 minutes per game. She put up consistent numbers before the Olympic break but was slightly more unreliable after the Sun acquired Marina Mabrey. Following an offseason trade, Harris will return to Dallas, where she spent the first three years of her career. She'll play alongside DiJonai Carrington, who was also her teammate in Connecticut, along with superstar guard Arike Ogunbowale. The Wings are also expected to select guard Paige Bueckers with the first overall pick in this year's draft, which may not leave much fantasy-relevant work for Harris. Although she had an encouraging performance last year, Harris will likely have trouble replicating those results in 2025.

When healthy, Sabally had a fairly consistent role for the Liberty in 2024, averaging 13.5 minutes per game across 26 appearances. She showed flashes of potential, including a 14-point, 10-rebound double-double against the Sparks on Aug. 28, one of only two times she played 20-plus minutes in a game. New York lost Kayla Thornton and Courtney Vandersloot this offseason and didn't make any notable acquisitions outside of Cheyenne Parker-Tyus while other stars around the league swapped teams, leaving Sabally to operate as the primary backup to Jonquel Jones again. Sabally can contribute in fantasy if she sees 20-plus minutes, but she's not expected to have that role when everyone is healthy in 2025.

James was a strong scoring threat over her four seasons at NC State, and she was selected by the Wings at the end of the first round of this year's draft. The 22-year-old fits well with the Wings' style of play but will likely struggle to find opportunities behind Arike Ogunbowale and No. 1 pick Paige Bueckers, while new acquisitions DiJonai Carrington and Tyasha Harris could also be prioritized in the rotation. James is a threat from the perimeter, as she shot 33.8 percent on 6.1 three-point attempts per game over her final two seasons with the Wolfpack. This could help her provide a spark off the bench, but it seems unlikely that James will have enough playing time as a rookie to be a fantasy-relevant option.

Amihere was the eighth overall pick by Atlanta in the 2023 WNBA Draft, but she struggled to enter the team's rotation over the first two years of her career. Over her first two seasons in the league, she averaged 2.0 points and 1.4 assists in 6.1 minutes per game. She was waived by Atlanta in February and subsequently claimed by the Valkyries. Golden State focused on several international prospects during offseason activities, but Amihere was waived by the Valkyries ahead of the regular season, even after she played double-digit minutes in each of the team's two preseason games. She could draw interest from other teams in 2025, but her fantasy upside seems limited.

Despite starting in just two of her 40 regular-season appearances in 2024, Walker-Kimbrough put together one of her best professional seasons in her fourth year with the Mystics. She averaged a career-high 7.5 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 22.1 minutes per game, and while she had some strong fantasy performances, her bench role made her more of a streaming candidate in most fantasy formats. Walker-Kimbrough signed a one-year deal with Atlanta ahead of her age-30 season, and it seems unlikely that she'll earn a consistent starting role with her new team, especially after the Dream acquired Brittney Griner and Brionna Jones during the offseason. Walker-Kimbrough tends to see fairly consistent playing time while operating as a reserve, but her production will likely be inconsistent if she can't secure a starting job.

Samuelson struggled to find a consistent role early in her career, but she's appeared in 63 games across the last two seasons while putting together solid production for the Sparks and Mystics. Over 29 appearances (19 starts) for Washington last year, she averaged 8.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 24.6 minutes per game, which made her a fairly consistent fantasy option. However, Samuelson lost out on her starting job over the final few months of the season, and she was traded to the Lynx in mid-April. It's unlikely that she'll be able to carve out as much playing time with her new team, and she'll likely have to settle for a bench role behind Napheesa Collier and Bridget Carleton. Samuelson's production over the last two seasons made her an intriguing late-round fantasy option, but she profiles more as a streaming candidate ahead of the 2025 campaign.

After averaging 9.4 minutes per game and falling out of the rotation several times for the Sky last season, Turner landed a spot with Indiana during the offseason. The Fever lost NaLyssa Smith over the winter but added Natasha Howard, DeWanna Bonner and Sophie Cunningham to a frontcourt that still has Aliyah Boston at the top, leaving little room for Turner in the rotation. In five seasons with Phoenix before moving to Chicago, Turner averaged at least 26 minutes per game four times and at least 31 minutes twice. She has plenty of experience but likely won't have a strong enough role for the revamped Fever to deliver consistent fantasy production.

DeShields didn't play in 2023 due to a knee injury, but she returned to the court with Chicago in 2024. She had success with the Sky over the first four years of her career and started in her first 10 appearances last season, but she shifted to a bench role in mid-June and had sporadic fantasy results down the stretch. Over 32 appearances (10 starts), she averaged 4.5 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 13.8 minutes per game, all of which were the worst marks of her career. She joined Connecticut during the offseason but missed both of the team's preseason games due to an ankle injury and was ultimately left off the Opening Night roster. She could provide a veteran presence in another locker room, but she's unlikely to have much fantasy value if she has to settle for a bench role elsewhere.

Barker had a somewhat slow start to her college career over her first three seasons, but she had a prominent role at Alabama over the last two years and was selected by the Sparks with the ninth pick in this year's draft. Barker has the ability to attack the rim, and she improved her perimeter shooting over the past two seasons, converting 36.3 percent of her three-point attempts while averaging 17.5 points to go with 6.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.0 steals in 30.8 minutes per game. The Sparks acquired Kelsey Plum during the offseason to play alongside Dearica Hamby, Rickea Jackson, Cameron Brink and Azura Stevens, and Barker could be forced to compete for bench minutes to begin her rookie season. However, Barker showed an ability to improve in college, so it wouldn't be surprising to see her role grow throughout the 2025 campaign, but she still seems unlikely to be more than a streaming candidate in most fantasy formats given the talent around her.

After two seasons in Los Angeles, Talbot was selected by the Valkyries during the WNBA Expansion Draft this offseason. She's never averaged more than 18 minutes per game across her six-year WNBA career, but the 30-year-old has a clear path to a consistent starting role in a frontcourt featuring Kayla Thornton, Monique Billings and Temi Fagbenle. Known as a sharpshooter, Talbot shot a career-low 26.0 percent from deep on 1.4 three-point attempts per game last season, her first WNBA action since tearing her ACL while playing overseas ahead of the 2023 campaign. Despite the poor shooting numbers in 2024, Talbot still holds a 36.6 percent mark from three in her career and could be a fantasy contributor if she earns a 25-plus-minute role for the WNBA's newest team, which will likely be led statistically by Tiffany Hayes and Julie Vanloo.

Brown has been productive when on the court over the past two seasons, but her availability has been limited after she was diagnosed with Crohn's disease midway through the 2023 campaign. She's appeared in just 28 games over the last two years, averaging 10.3 points, 2.8 assists and 2.2 rebounds in 27.0 minutes per game across the span. The 30-year-old was traded to the Storm during the offseason, and if she's healthy this spring, she'll likely compete with Erica Wheeler for a starting role ahead of the 2025 campaign. Even if Brown earns a starting role, her limited availability in recent years makes her a risky fantasy option.

Uzun made her WNBA debut in 2024 and served as a starter for the struggling Wings in her first 18 appearances of the season. She had consistent fantasy output during that time, averaging 6.8 points, 4.4 assists and 2.4 rebounds in 29.6 minutes per game. However, the 27-year-old lost her starting job at the end of June and had inconsistent playing time down the stretch. She averaged just 2.4 points and 1.8 assists in 13.0 minutes per game over her final 22 appearances of the year and will get a fresh start in 2025 after being traded to the Mercury in January. The 27-year-old will likely compete with Sami Whitcomb for a starting role following Diana Taurasi's retirement, but Uzun's upside would be limited considerably if she comes off the bench.

After starting 27 of 38 games as a rookie in 2023, Juhasz saw a reduced role in 2024 as Minnesota made a run to the WNBA Finals. The Lynx are essentially running it back with the same roster in 2025, but Juhasz announced just before the start of the regular season that she'll miss the 2025 campaign due to personal reasons. Jessica Shepard, Bridget Carleton and Karlie Samuelson are candidates to see increased roles this year, while Juhasz's next chance to suit up for the Lynx will be in 2026.

After seven seasons in Seattle, Russell signed with Los Angeles this offseason. The veteran has played more than 20 minutes per game only twice over her eight-year career and not since 2021. With Cameron Brink likely unavailable for at least the start of 2025 due to a knee injury, Russell should be able to carve out a rotational role in the Sparks' frontcourt. However, she'll likely be behind Rickea Jackson, Dearica Hamby and maybe even Azura Stevens. When Russell is seeing 20-plus minutes, she can provide fantasy value, but she's unlikely to have that type of role consistently with the Sparks.

Miller had a significant decline in playing time and production in 2024 while dealing with a lingering knee injury. After losing to the Liberty in the WNBA Finals, the Lynx are essentially running it back with the same roster in 2025, leaving Miller to operate off the bench behind Napheesa Collier, Alanna Smith and Bridget Carleton while competing for minutes with Dorka Juhasz. With Kayla McBride, Courtney Williams and Collier leading the team in usage, Miller will have a tough time consistently producing enough to make a fantasy impact.

Samuelson mainly served as a starter with the Storm and Sparks during the 2021 and 2022 seasons, respectively, but she was unavailable in 2023 due to her pregnancy. She returned to the court with the Fever last year but started in just 15 of her 37 regular-season appearances. The 27-year-old wasn't very productive regardless of her starting status, and she averaged just 4.3 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 18.2 minutes per game. Samuelson mutually parted ways with Indiana in February and joined Seattle ahead of the 2025 season, but she sustained a torn ACL that will force her to miss the 2025 campaign. She'll face a lengthy recovery process ahead of the 2026 season.

Amoore is an undersized rookie at 5-foot-6, but she had plenty of success in college between Virginia Tech and Kentucky. Over her final three collegiate seasons -- two of which were with the Hokies and one of which was with the Wildcats -- she averaged 18.2 points, 6.2 assists and 2.6 rebounds in 36.1 minutes per game. The Australian is known as a hardworking player and should have an opportunity to compete for a role with the Mystics early in her career, but she suffered an ACL injury in April that will force her to miss the 2025 campaign. Amoore should have chances to develop in the future, but she faces a lengthy recovery process during her rookie season.

Jocyte is just 19 years old, but she's had success overseas in recent seasons and was selected by the Valkyries with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. She joins the WNBA's newest franchise, an organization that targeted plenty of international talent via the expansion draft over the winter. While playing alongside No. 2 pick Dominique Malonga with French club Lyon in the BWL this season, Jocyte averaged 11.9 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 28.2 minutes per game. While she's a solid shooter with decent size, her availability is in question, as she's expressed that her top priority is playing for the Lithuanian national team, and they'll be playing in EuroBasket in June. She'll at least be unavailable for the first half of the season while preparing for international play and isn't expected to join the Valkyries in 2025.

The Fever acquired Brown and Sophie Cunningham in a four-team trade this offseason. Last year, Brown shined during the preseason but made only 14 regular-season appearances for the Wings during an injury-plagued campaign. Her path to playing time is bleaker than it was in Dallas, as she'll now have to compete for bench minutes with Lexie Hull and Sophie Cunningham, both capable starters in the WNBA. Also, when healthy, Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, Natasha Howard, DeWanna Bonner and Aliyah Boston will dominate the playing time and usage, leaving Brown as an afterthought in fantasy.

Holmes has been an inconsistent fantasy option in recent years, but she signed a training camp contract with the Wings during the offseason. Dallas experienced plenty of roster turnover this winter, losing Natasha Howard and Satou Sabally in the frontcourt, but the team added forwards NaLyssa Smith and Myisha Hines-Allen while also drafting guard Paige Bueckers with the No. 1 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. Holmes has played for the Sun, Sparks and Storm over the past three seasons, and she averaged 3.1 points and 2.2 rebounds in 9.7 minutes per game during that time. While she could see a slightly larger role with the new-look Wings, it seems unlikely that the 27-year-old will be a reliable fantasy contributor.

After being selected by the Sky with the No. 10 pick in this year's draft, Sivka joins a Sky frontcourt that includes Angel Reese and Kamilla Cardoso. Sivka is a 6-foot-4 forward but is a capable perimeter shooter who should be able to provide a spark off the bench once she plays in the WNBA. The Sky conversed with the Slovenian during the draft process, but she plans to remain overseas in 2025 before joining the Sky in 2026. Sivka is an intriguing long-term prospect for Chicago with international experience, but she'll wait before making her WNBA debut.

Dojkic had some strong performances with the Storm in 2023, averaging 6.5 points and 2.8 assists in 20.0 minutes per game over 23 regular-season appearances (15 starts). She joined the Liberty in 2024, but her production took a step back, as she averaged just 3.3 points in 9.9 minutes per game over 26 regular-season outings, all of which came off the bench. She'll return to New York in 2025 after being designated as a reserved player, and she could compete for additional playing time in the backcourt since Betnijah Laney-Hamilton will miss most of the season, but the Liberty also traded for Natasha Cloud during the offseason after losing Courtney Vandersloot. Dojkic will compete with Marine Johannes for off the bench but will still likely serve mainly as a streaming option in most fantasy formats following her lackluster first season with the Liberty.

After a somewhat consistent role for Indiana over the first half of the 2024 season, Wallace wasn't part of the Fever's rotation following the Olympic break. She finished with season-long averages of 4.7 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 0.7 steals in 17.2 minutes per game across 26 appearances (15 starts). Indiana looks revamped ahead of Year 2 with Caitlin Clark, replacing NaLyssa Smith with DeWanna Bonner, Natasha Howard and Sophie Cunningham, but Kristy Wallace has elected to sit out the 2025 WNBA season. It's unclear whether she intends to return in 2026.

Parks spent the 2023 season with the Sky, averaging 3.9 points and 1.6 rebounds in 13.6 minutes per game across 37 regular-season appearances (two starts). She received a reserved qualifying offer from Chicago ahead of the 2024 campaign but didn't return to the club before the team renounced her rights. However, she received a qualifying offer from the Sun during the offseason and made the team's Opening Night roster, even after Connecticut selected Aneesah Morrow in the first round of this year's draft. When the team is fully healthy, Parks will likely need to settle for a bench role behind Morrow and Olivia Nelson-Ododa. However, Parks could step in as a starter when needed and has some streaming value in fantasy since the Sun waived Diamond DeShields ahead of the regular season.
